redCandidate.publicEntry: resolveCatalogEntries() for an AIOS-managed client and scope
redCandidate.setup: Pass two catalog entries with distinct canonical sources but the same client, scope, and installed Provider skill name. Both source directories exist in the checked-in canonical skill tree.

args: import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { resolveCatalogEntries } from './scripts/lib/components/skills/catalog.mjs'; const catalog=[{name:'duplicate-provider',source:'skill-sources/aios-codemap-ops',clients:['codex'],scopes:['global']},{name:'duplicate-provider',source:'skill-sources/aios-interception-runtime',clients:['codex'],scopes:['global']}]; assert.throws(() => resolveCatalogEntries({rootDir:process.cwd(),catalog,clientName:'codex',scope:'global',selectedSkills:[],manifest:null}), /duplicate-provider/);

redCandidate.expected: An ambiguous same-name target is rejected with an error that identifies duplicate-provider instead of yielding a first-match result.
redCandidate.observed: The recorded scenario exited with status 1 because resolveCatalogEntries() returned both entries without rejecting the ambiguity, so the assertion that it throws failed.
redCandidate.failureReason: Catalog selection preserves manifest enumeration order and has no duplicate target-key analysis. Downstream installation could therefore overwrite one source with another without an explicit precedence contract.
